# intl-divergences.txt js-n3c-cldr-ci-ubuntu: row N3c: Other locales' currency patterns and symbols: `fr`, `es`, `pt-PT`, `ko-KR`, `zh-TW`, `sv`, `ar`; Broiler.JS answers the package's and the host's: `fr` `"-1 234,50 U+20AC"`, `"1,00 $US"`; `ko-KR` `"US$1.00"`; `ar` `"-1U+066C234U+066B50U+20AC"`; data policy (C5): its embedding takes CLDR 48.2.0 for every locale of decision D5's list; on the CI host of run 40400894567's job 121846364071, `engine vectors (ubuntu-latest)`, Ubuntu 26.04.1 (image `ubuntu-26.04` 20261012.163.1), whose ICU is 78.2 by the image's software list (`libicu-dev` 78.2-2ubuntu1; the job's log names none), Broiler.JS's answer follows that ICU, not the pinned CLDR: `en-FR` `EUR` -1234.5 `"-U+20AC1U+202F234,50"`; the vector matches on the host revision 28's first runs were taken on (Ubuntu 24.04.5, ICU 74.2), where a run reports this divergence as no longer holding; from SJL-9.5, this engine's cut-over to the shared Intl library, Broiler.JS answers that data on a host that lists `en-FR` (decision D7, revision 35), and CLDR 48.2.0's answer is not out: `en-FR` inherits `en-150`'s currency pattern `#,##0.00U+00A0U+00A4` (cldr-core's parentLocales; common/main/en_FR.xml has no currency formats) with its own decimal `,` and group U+202F, `"-1U+202F234,50U+00A0U+20AC"` by that data; the owner's decision of 2026-11-08 ("Revision 36: follow CLDR") accepts the pinned data's answer, so no task answers it: this engine's record is data policy C5 and that decision, with the dated note of 2026-11-09 under SJL-9's data changes (C5) in docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md; on a host that lists no `en-FR`, as ICU 74.2 does not, Broiler.JS resolves it to `en` (row L29) and matches

# regexp-divergences.txt js-m2a: row M2a: the dotted and dotless i, i and I against U+0130 and U+0131, in literals, classes and back-references, without u; Broiler.JS answers, under tr-TR, true for i and U+0130 and for I and U+0131, and under lt-LT true for i and I against U+0130, with the negated classes false: RegexOptions.IgnoreCase without CultureInvariant reads .NET's current culture; under the invariant culture it answers as Canonicalize does, and a run there reports the field as no longer holding; a correction of Broiler.JS (JSD-0081; decision D33, its bundle sjl-11-001's part D); answered by SJL-11.5, Broiler.JS's cut-over to Broiler.Regex

# regexp-divergences.txt vm-s9b: row S9b: a literal ending in a backslash at the end of eval code, /a[bc\, by direct and indirect eval; Broiler.VM answers an EvalError ("the artifact provider did not supply a program"): the scan moves past the end of the source (CP/SliceTokenizer.cs:2227 at aaa39fb); a correction of Broiler.VM outside SJL-11 (JSD-0081: the scanner is the front end's, SJL-12's and SJL-13's); answered by the front end's cut-over to the shared syntax library (SJL-13), not by SJL-11.4

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-d32: row D32: `new.target` in a class field initialiser at function depth 0 (alone, or in an arrow in it); Broiler.VM answers refused 2101 at `new`: ParseFieldTail parses the initialiser without raising functionDepth, so ParseNewTarget refuses; a correction of Broiler.VM (JSD-0083); answered by step 1 of SJL-13.3, Broiler.VM's wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-p15b: row P15b: a parenthesised nested target that is not a simple target, `({ a: (b = 7) } = ...)`, `({ a: ([b]) } = ...)`; Broiler.VM answers accepted: the parenthesised set is consulted only for the whole left-hand side; a correction of Broiler.VM (JSD-0083); answered by step 1 of SJL-13.3, Broiler.VM's wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-p31: row P31: an AssignmentRestProperty whose target is an object or array literal, `({...{a}} = o)`, `({...[a]} = o)`; Broiler.VM answers accepted (the rest object is destructured, so with an array literal it throws a TypeError when it runs); a correction of both (JSD-0083); answered for Broiler.VM by step 1 of SJL-13.3, its wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-t13: row T13: ASCII white space inside `\x`/`\u` escapes; Broiler.VM answers accepted on the wide path: .NET's HexNumber parses allow leading and trailing white space, so `"\x 1"`, `"\x1 "`, `"\u 041"` and `"\x<LF>1"` are accepted; a correction of Broiler.VM (JSD-0083); answered by step 1 of SJL-13.3, Broiler.VM's wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-t16: row T16: strict refusal of legacy octal integer literals in object keys and class element names; Broiler.VM answers strict `{ 010: 1 }` accepted, class `010(){}` accepted, function-strict key accepted: PropertyKey's numeric arm has no legacy-octal check; a correction of both (JSD-0083), Broiler.VM's for a legacy octal object key or class element name in strict code; answered for Broiler.VM by step 1 of SJL-13.3, its wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-t24d: row T24d: a regular expression after a `for await (...)` head; Broiler.VM answers refused: a head needs if, while, for or with before `(`, so after `await` a `/` is division; a correction of both (JSD-0083); answered for Broiler.VM by step 1 of SJL-13.3, its wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-t24e: row T24e: a regular expression after a prefix `++` or `--`; Broiler.VM answers refused: PlusPlus and MinusMinus read division; a correction of both (JSD-0083); answered for Broiler.VM by step 1 of SJL-13.3, its wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-t24f: row T24f: a division after `await` used as an identifier in a Script; Broiler.VM answers refused: Await falls to a regular expression, and where `;` or the end of input follows the literal too, refused 2102 at the regular expression (1:36), an answer the row records since 2026-10-27 from a probe (decision D-t24); a correction of both (JSD-0083); answered for Broiler.VM by step 1 of SJL-13.3, its wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-t6: row T6: `#!` and `-->` right after a substitution's `${`; Broiler.VM answers accepted (`${#!<LF>1}` and `${--><LF>1}` are `1`): each substitution is read by an inner tokenizer whose text starts after `${`, which treats it as a source start; a correction of Broiler.VM (JSD-0083); answered by step 1 of SJL-13.3, Broiler.VM's wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-t7: row T7: the template-end scan and HTML-like comments in a substitution; Broiler.VM answers `${1 <!-- }<LF>}` is `"1\n}"` (a different template, no error): the scan has no arm for `<!--` or `-->`, so a `}` inside one closes the substitution; a correction of Broiler.VM (JSD-0083); answered by step 1 of SJL-13.3, Broiler.VM's wide path on the shared syntax library

# syntax-divergences.txt vm-t8: row T8: the template-end scan's regular-expression-or-division guess; Broiler.VM answers `${typeof /}/}` refused 2006 and `${...return /`/...}` refused 2007: after `typeof` and `return` a `/` is division, so a `}` or a backquote in the literal ends the substitution or opens a template (the vectors hold the `}` in a character class, `${typeof /[}]/}`, which needs no Annex B, and the backquote after `return`); a correction of Broiler.VM (JSD-0083); answered by step 1 of SJL-13.3, Broiler.VM's wide path on the shared syntax library

# intl-divergences.txt js-p3: row P3: Which languages' rules each engine holds: fr, ru, pl, cs, uk, hi, he, ar, cy, ja, pt, pt-PT (cardinal) ...; data policy (C5): its embedding takes CLDR 48.2.0 for every locale of decision D5's list; since SJL-9.5, this engine's cut-over to the shared Intl library (Broiler-Platform/Broiler.JS#1110, merged as a5f2692e), Broiler.JS's plural and ordinal rules are CLDR 48.2.0's for every language CLDR states rules for, and CLDR 48.2.0 states none for `sa` (cldr-core's supplemental/plurals.json and ordinals.json; the data home's plurals.txt and ordinals.txt have no `sa` line), so Broiler.JS answers root's one category, `["other"]` cardinal and ordinal, and `other` for every number, where out is the reference's answer (ICU 78.3, CLDR 48.0), which holds no rules for `sa` either: its PluralRules lists no `sa` (`Intl.PluralRules.supportedLocalesOf(["sa"])` is `[]`) and resolves `sa` to the default locale `en-US` (`resolvedOptions().locale`), so out is `en-US`'s categories, cardinal `["one","other"]` and ordinal `["one","two","few","other"]`, and `en-US`'s cardinal selection, `one` for 1 and `other` for the rest; Broiler.JS/CHANGELOG.md lists it among SJL-9.5's "Answers that still differ from the corpus's expectation", under this row; no task answers it: the difference is the pinned data's answer for a language it states no rules for against the reference's default-locale fallback, the kind of difference the owner's decision of 2026-11-08 ("Revision 36: follow CLDR") settled for `gv` and `ln` under row S1b (js-s1b-cldr), whose ListFormat the reference also resolves to `en-US`, by accepting the pinned data's answer; that decision and revision 36 name those two data facts and not `sa`'s, so whether it covers this one too, which would make this engine's record data policy C5 and that decision, as js-s1b-cldr's is, is the owner's to decide

# intl-divergences.txt js-u15-d34: row U15: Unit and list patterns: `long` `{hours: 1, minutes: 2}` in `fr`, `ja`, `es`, `ar`, `zh-TW` ...; data policy (C5): its embedding takes CLDR 48.2.0 for every locale of decision D5's list; since SJL-9.5, this engine's cut-over to the shared Intl library (Broiler-Platform/Broiler.JS#1110, merged as a5f2692e), Broiler.JS writes `af` and `lt` `{hours: 1, minutes: 2, seconds: 3}` in the `long` style as the clock `"01:02:03"`, row U14's answer (two-digit hours), not this row's: [[TwoDigitHours]] is true for both in Broiler.JS's data, and the shared library's GetDurationUnitOptions makes the hours `2-digit` whatever style they resolved, and the minutes and seconds after them, as ECMA-402 at 3d4c558 writes the step (spec/durationformat.html:615); the owner's decision of 2026-11-02, under decision D34 (Broiler.ECMAScript/CHANGELOG.md, stage SJL-9.3f's note: the library follows the pinned text as written), settles that answer, and Broiler.JS/CHANGELOG.md lists `af` and `lt` `"01:02:03"` among SJL-9.5's data changes under row U14, and also lists these two vectors among its "Answers that still differ from the corpus's expectation", under this row ("duration unit and list patterns (U15) of `af`, ... and `lt`"); this reason is headed by U15, the only row the vectors' notes name, and not by U14, the row whose answer Broiler.JS gives, so it does not meet this file's rule for the row a difference is classified under, which is the owner's to settle with the expectation below; meanwhile these vectors' per-engine expectation, which is out, keeps the words, `"1 uur, 2 minute, 3 sekondes"` and `"1 valanda 2 minutU+0117s ir 3 sekundU+0117s"`; no task answers it: this engine's record is decision D34 and the owner's decision of 2026-11-02, under which the expectation is the owner's to read again (Broiler.ECMAScript/CHANGELOG.md: "SJL-9.5 lists the move under decision D34, or the owner restricts the step to `numeric` hours by a dated decision made in both engines")

# regexp-divergences.txt js-b8: row B8 as revised 2026-11-01 (owner's decision D-p5): a flat sequence of 100,000 (?:a) under u on 100,000 a; Broiler.JS answers, since its u patterns went to Broiler.Regex 0.1.0-preview.5 (a58d31d1), the whole input after about 4 s evaluated alone on the runs' host, a time that grows about as the square of the length, so a run beside other runs renders the runner's abort at its 5 s limit (each of the four first runs did), where the row recorded a process abort, a stack overflow in Matcher.ReadAt, under preview.4; the difference this field classifies is the runner's 5 s limit, not the row's class (a correction of Broiler.JS and of Broiler.Regex's preview.4, JSD-0081's R4, no CLR recursion in the matcher), which preview.5 already meets, since the process no longer aborts; the time is not attributed here, nothing yet shows that SJL-11.5, Broiler.JS's cut-over to Broiler.Regex, removes it, and its classification stays open for the owner; the vector so breaks SCHEMA.md section 7's premise that a runner's limit is far above any vector's time, which a later revision may restore by a smaller input
